label: first copy step fed back h (sequence starts with h)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely (99% of mass) at step L+1. That is the step where the fed-back first original token is the input and the model outputs original token 1. Strong activations (up to 5.4) happen only when that first token is h; on dev, the predicate has precision 1.0 and mass recall 0.91, and it covers all of the top two activation quartiles. When step L+1 has a different input, the feature often fires weakly (about 0.01-0.1 of max; y, m, 1 and x are somewhat more common). There are also rare weak activations at step L+2 when the input is h. Never fires during the original phase, at the delimiter, at later copy steps, or on an h that appears anywhere other than right after DEL.

issues: All factual claims hold on test: the predicate gets precision 1.0 (no false positives in dev or test), recall 0.447, F1 0.618 and mass recall 0.913. The profile shows zero activity in the original phase and at the delimiter. In the copy phase the feature fires only at recall_idx 1 (99.3% of mass) and recall_idx 2 (0.7%).

The leftover 8.7% of mass is weak firing at recall_idx 1 on any input token (relative activation about 0.01-0.1), with no single dominant token. This is a diffuse baseline at the same step, not a separate class. recall_idx==1 alone has mass recall 0.993 but precision only 0.07, so it is not a better predicate.
The recall_idx 2 & h activations are minor: precision 0.10, mass recall 0.007.

Minor wording issue: 'first copy step' means the first step where a fed-back token is the input (step L+1). Strictly, the first copy-phase step is the DEL step L, but the explanation states the step clearly, so this is not an overclaim. The label's parenthetical is also loose: the feature responds to h as the fed-back input at L+1, which means the original sequence started with h.
